The bus API, measured at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py:433: bus.read(*, to=None, channel=None, reply_to=None) -> list[dict] — every record addressed to 'to' on 'channel', flushed DB rows first then ring rows, insertion order preserved, so the LAST element is the newest. Each record is a dict with a 'body' key (a dict, or a JSON string after a DB round-trip — json.loads it when str). 'announce' is a declared channel; bus.post(sender=d, to=d, channel='announce', why=..., body={'verbs': [...]}) writes one, which is exactly what BaseShim._announce_menu (cairn/tools/base/shim.py) posts at wiring and what the proof's scratch bus (BusDevice.scratch) posts. So token.roster walks bus.read(to=d, channel='announce') in reverse, takes the first record whose body carries a list 'verbs', and includes d when 'sleep' is in it; records with no 'verbs' list (hands, closes) are skipped.
